newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's MICEX extends trading, adds new shares.
newsitem.headline: Russia's MICEX extends trading, adds new shares.

text.p: Russia's Moscow Interbank Currency Exchange (MICEX) said on Wednesday it will introduce an evening trading session in shares from July 22 because of growing turnover on the exchange.
It also said it had listed new shares from July 15.
"The market is growing, the volume is rising and it is getting more difficult for operators to watch the market within such a short period of time," MICEX expert Alexander Gerasimov told Reuters.

The new evening session will take place from 4.30 to 6.15 p.m. (1230 to 1415 GMT in summer, 1330 to 1515 GMT in winter), MICEX said in a statement. The exchange currently trades from 11 a.m. to 1 p.m. (0700-0900/0800-1000 GMT).
The exchange said it had started trading preferred shares of Russia's biggest oil company LUKoil, Rostelekom and Norilsk Nickel. It was already trading ordinary shares in the three companies.
It also started trading ordinary shares of Komineft, Noyabrskneftegaz, Tatneft oil companies, GUM retailer and Tomskenergo power utility, it said.
The bulk of share trading in Russia is done through the Russian Trading System, an electronic screen market similar to the U.S. NASDAQ.

MICEX, the main floor for government securities trading, and an important currency trading exchange, introduced equities trading in spring. Average daily turnover in equities has risen to 25 billion roubles ($4.33 million) from 2.5 billion roubles in March.
